headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading error: ms-swift can write local artifacts while Perplexity ingests uploaded content and browser context, creating a default path for sensitive data to flow into external search-backed outputs.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ms-swift can write files and emit logs/configuration/training outputs, while Perplexity can ingest uploaded documents and browsing context. If ms-swift-generated content is copied into Perplexity, prompt-like instructions can ride along. No shared channel is documented, so this is inferred rather than proven.
conditions: IF ms-swift outputs are pasted or uploaded into Perplexity as source material
IF Perplexity treats uploaded text or browsing context as instruction-bearing content
mitigations: Strip instructions from ms-swift outputs before upload
Use a fixed prompt template in Perplexity
Review uploaded files for embedded directives
Separate raw artifacts from analysis notes
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between the agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: ms-swift handles hub_token and sdk-token and can read/write local files; Perplexity accepts uploaded PDFs/images and sends queries to vendor APIs. If the same workspace contains secrets or sensitive support data, those contents can be uploaded into Perplexity’s vendor-hosted backend. The pairwise path is plausible but not directly documented.
conditions: IF secrets or customer data are present in files accessible to ms-swift
IF those files are uploaded or summarized through Perplexity
mitigations: Keep secrets out of shared folders
Redact tokens before analysis
Use a separate workspace for Perplexity uploads
Limit uploads to non-sensitive excerpts
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on upload paths

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ms-swift can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses, but Perplexity is vendor-hosted and cannot write the host filesystem or modify git state. Their write surfaces do not overlap, so direct resource conflict is limited. Uncertainty remains about shared workspace conventions, so I do not mark none.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same host directory
IF an external orchestrator mirrors Perplexity outputs back into local files
mitigations: Use separate directories per agent
Avoid concurrent edits to the same files
Keep Perplexity outputs read-only
Serialize any file handoff
requires-engineering: add locking around shared workspaces

D_cascading_error.rationale: Perplexity is a search-RAG system that produces cited answers, and ms-swift can generate training/evaluation outputs and configuration data. If ms-swift output is fed into Perplexity without verification, Perplexity may present or act on incorrect upstream content as authoritative. The interaction is plausible in default workflows but not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF ms-swift outputs are used as source material for Perplexity answers
IF no human or automated verification step checks the upstream output
mitigations: Verify ms-swift outputs before reuse
Cross-check cited claims against primary sources
Mark generated artifacts as untrusted
Use Perplexity only for retrieval, not final authority
requires-engineering: add validation gates between agents

E_compliance.rationale: ms-swift touches datasets, checkpoints, logs, and secrets, while Perplexity stores uploaded documents and browsing context in a vendor-hosted service. If regulated or sensitive support data is moved from ms-swift-managed local artifacts into Perplexity uploads, retention and residency obligations may diverge. The profiles do not specify a direct residency mismatch, so this is a policy-gap risk rather than a proven violation.
conditions: IF regulated customer data is included in ms-swift artifacts
IF those artifacts are uploaded to Perplexity or retained in its browsing context
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from uploads
Review retention settings before use
Delete uploaded files after analysis
Use anonymized samples only
requires-engineering: align retention and residency policies
